agent.problem: The earlier cards give no basis for knowing who was around Job, and children, servants and neighbors all fit the sentence. The baker can only select the unseen word children by luck rather than reason out the blank's meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The wrong answer A hard life surrounded by enemies is not false everywhere in the passage. In Job 30:12-14, Job describes the rabble laying snares, building siege ramps and advancing against him, so this option resembles his present suffering even though it was not what he expected in Job 29:18.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

agent.problem: Several choice cards rely on referents from cards that are no longer on screen: card 2 says these young men, card 4 says they, card 5 says these men and card 11 says that mud. The questions should restate enough context, such as identifying the younger men who mock Job and saying that God has thrown Job into the mud.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

agent.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason that the mockery comes in song rather than letters or court. All three options fit, so this blank tests unseen wording and luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The walkthrough jumps from Job 30:21-23 on card 13 to Job 30:25 here, leaving Job 30:24 entirely untold. That verse is a distinct step in Job's complaint: no one stretches out his hand against a ruined man when he cries for help. Omitting it loses part of the flow into Job's appeal to his own compassion.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: This story card tells both the earlier detail about God's lamp shining above Job's head from Job 29:3 and the new statement from Job 30:26, but it cites only Job 30:26. Its citation does not cover all the Scripture the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: Answering False only establishes that Job's skin is not starting to heal. Neither this card nor any other tells what Job 30:30 actually says: his skin grows black and peels, and his bones burn with fever. The closing picture of his physical affliction is therefore not actually taught.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

human.problem: This last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from any verse, but it cites Job 30:31. Card 19 already cites that verse. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, which here is none.
human.question: What should a last story card cite when it is only the 'story continues' line and tells no verse? The last verse of the passage, the passage's whole range, or nothing?
